P1.evidence: All four moves ran cleanly. Read back the application — 'I read through your application, so I have a pretty good head start on where you're at with things' — and used it to confirm his age. Delivered the full four-part frame verbatim in substance: 'where you're at today, where you want to go, what's been getting in the way and what you genuinely need to get there.' Took frame agreement, 'that sound good?' → 'Yeah, that sounds great.' Then the open question: 'what could we potentially help you with today, man? Again, I read your application, but I want to kind of just hear everything from you personally.'

P2.evidence: Rep explicitly flagged the baseline block — 'I want to establish a little bit of baseline with you, man... I'm just going to go through a list of questions here' — and worked it methodically. Height and weight asked directly, age confirmed off the application. Work covered including the desk-bound question: 'Your job, I'm assuming you're sitting most of the day, is that right?' Injuries asked directly and followed up properly on the pectoral: 'just to clarify, the right peck, that was a tear, you said?' Training week, diet, sleep and energy all asked. P2c is partial because the cancer, diabetes and hypertension history was volunteered unprompted in the prospect's opening monologue and the rep never asked the health-conditions question — he only later referenced it as already covered ('I know we talked about health conditions, but any like injuries...') and ran a catch-all at the end. Nothing hereditary was asked beyond what the prospect offered about his mother. P2f partial: the rep reflected results back ('as far as physique, I know we said we weren't super happy with that') rather than asking what results the current training had produced.

P3.evidence: The deep-goal work was the strongest part of the call. The bridge landed hard — 'You're seven years old, and most dudes in their 70 are just kicking back... what's the drive behind it for you? Like, why are we so motivated to figure this out?' — and produced the granddaughter, the son and the legacy material. The future-pace ran too: 'let's say it's six months from now... walk me through what else changes in your life.' Marked down because several moves were reflected rather than asked. P3a: the one-thing-you'd-change question was never put; the rep summarised. P3c: the things he wants to do but can't (swim, ride the bikes, run a mile flat out) were volunteered inside the future-pace, not elicited by the scripted question. P3f: 'who else does that impact?' was never asked — the prospect offered the granddaughter himself and the rep engaged with a joke rather than a question. P3h: the reflect-back was aimed at the mechanism, 'it's not for lack of motivation or commitment, it's just we need a system that works for you', not at the deeper why. The rep had legacy, mortality and a 7-year-old granddaughter on the table and never mirrored it back.

P4.evidence: Root cause was reached but by the prospect's route, not the script's. The rep's question — 'you mentioned you keep falling short despite consistency and discipline. Like, what do you feel is actually the biggest missing thing?' — covers P4c and P4d well, and the prospect named the gap himself: sleep, recovery, information overload and cookie-cutter programming. But 'what have you tried before?' and 'what happened with that?' were never asked as questions; the prospect volunteered the history of cookie-cutter programmes unprompted. P4f ran only in its soft form. The confrontational version — 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own?' — was replaced with 'we're looking for some sort of guidance, some sort of direction, and somebody who can tell us we're doing the right thing.' The rep did ask the good timing question, 'why is it now all of a sudden? Like, what changed where it's like, hey, I actually need some help?', which partially recovers this.

P5.evidence: This is the phase that broke, and it is the most actionable coaching point on the call. P5a was asked well: 'if we don't get that coaching, that clarity, that custom system for what's actually going to work for you, like what will life look like in a couple of years if we don't actually figure this thing out?' The prospect then deflected it completely — 'I don't think that I could hold anybody responsible for what my vision is of myself and my dream' — and talked for two minutes about variables and other people's encouragement without ever describing a negative future. The rep did not re-ask, did not follow with 'is that something you're willing to settle for?' and never asked 'why not?'. He jumped straight to P5d — 'it sounds like it might be time to draw a line in the sand and get the same fricking sorted once and for all' — which got a yes, but a yes with no cost of inaction underneath it. The consequence frame was therefore never actually built, and that is the likeliest reason the call ended in comparison shopping rather than a decision.

P6.evidence: Both commitment questions were asked and both got a clean 'Absolutely.' P6a: 'Do you feel like that's everything that you need to be lean, strong, flexible, and mobile from this point forward and into the future?' P6b: 'if we can figure out all the details, okay, are you... really fully committed to going all in, following the program, hitting the workouts the way they're prescribed, and really doing this thing to master this once and for all?' P6c is a clear miss. Hesitation surfaced within ninety seconds of the price — an active competitor and a request to defer to Monday — and the script says return to Phase 5. The rep did not return to Phase 5. He worked the comparison for fifteen minutes and then invented a $1,200 paid trial. The commitment was to the idea, not to the decision, and the difference was never tested.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted and payment collection was started: legal name, billing address, email and phone were all captured and the rep asked 'did you want to do Visa, MasterCard, Amex, what works best on that side of things?' The prospect deferred and no payment was taken, so step 1 failed. Steps 2 to 4 — the Trevor onboarding call, the agreement email signed on the call, and the welcome email / Skool link / onboarding questionnaire instructions — were never reached and are scored not applicable rather than missed.

objection_plays.detail: Trigger was a deferral to Monday and then a request for 24 hours. The rep ran the isolation move well — 'is there anything else that kind of needs to be figured out between now and Monday, or is it literally just deciding between the two of them?' — and got a clean isolate. From there almost nothing scripted ran. No 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal?', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here — when do you make a different decision?', and no 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now?'. That last one was sitting there for the taking given the granddaughter material. Instead the rep substituted a commercial concession for the play.

Trigger: 'I have to talk to my counterpart... she's the bad cop and I'm the good cop' and 'I will kick it around with her.' The rep ran three of the scripted moves — support check ('is she pretty supportive with you getting fitness dialed in?'), the reason-she-would-want-it move ('why do you feel like she wants you to be long, strong, lean, fit, healthy?') and the anticipate-obstacles move ('what do you think the potential concerns would be?'). He established she was supportive and had already guessed the price. He then abandoned the play. The two moves that decide this objection — 'is this genuinely needing her input, or asking permission to bet on yourself?' and 'this isn't a joint decision like buying a house, is that responsibility hers or yours?' — never ran, and the deposit fallback was not used as scripted.

Script gap, not a rep failure. The real objection on this call was a directly comparable competitor at a comparable price — Marcus Filly — where the prospect said 'you guys are really in the same ballpark in terms of time and finance' and 'it's not the commitment or the program or the money... Who do we go with?'. The playbook has five plays and all five assume the blocker is money, timing, a spouse, deliberation or fear. None of them addresses 'I have two credible providers and I like both.' The rep improvised competently for a while — isolating the difference down to kettlebell specialisation versus cross-training, which is genuinely Primal's strongest ground — but with no play to close on he reached for price architecture instead and invented a $1,200 one-month trial. This is the third documented instance of the playbook having no answer for a value-comparison objection and it should be written into the script.

notes: Excellent open and excellent deep-goal work, undone by two things. First, the consequence frame collapsed — the prospect deflected P5a and the rep never re-ran it, so there was no cost of inaction holding the close together when a competitor surfaced. Second, when hesitation appeared the rep discounted instead of returning to Phase 5, improvising a $1,200 entry price. Coach the P5 recovery specifically: when a prospect answers the two-year question with philosophy instead of a picture, ask it again and make it concrete. Also flag for the clinical conversation this call never had.
